In general, the Skip-gram objective predicts surrounding context words from a center (target) word: for each word, it maximizes the probability of each word within a fixed window around it, conditioned only on that center word, and the context words are treated as conditionally independent. A standard language-modeling objective instead predicts the next word from the preceding words (a left-to-right, autoregressive factorization, P(w_t | w_1...w_{t-1})). So Skip-gram goes from a center word to its neighbors in both directions, while language modeling goes from the past sequence to the next token. If Passage A and Passage B define these objectives differently, their specific formulations should take precedence over this general description.
